name: prose-research
description: Provenance for prose: a dossier of sources and quotable passages, a claims ledger with the writer's confidence, and deterministic checks of quotes, links and unledgered claims.

interface.shortDescription: Keeps a project's sources, passages and claims with provenance, and checks a draft's quotes, links and unledgered claims.
interface.longDescription: One skill. prose-research takes a source in (a URL fetched with Node's built-in fetch, a file, a PDF through pdftotext or a text export), proposes a dossier entry with the text's sha256 and retrieval instant, and stores it only on approval under the shared writing-identity registry, where cached source text lets a quote be checked later against what the source said then. A claims ledger records claim, source, location, exact quote and the writer's own confidence label, carried as confidence_by: writer so nothing reads it as a measurement. claims-check.mjs reports every ledger quote as exact, drifted or absent (whitespace is the only normalisation), every link as ok, dead or not-evaluated (offline is never ok), and every draft sentence the model's sentence map marks as a claim with no ledger entry. provenance-scan.mjs tells prose-review's fidelity critic which quote atoms drifted from their sources. Nothing here says a claim is true. NOTE: Codex runs the skill inline; use the bundle's AGENTS.md block so quotes are checked by the script rather than asserted from memory.
defaultPrompt: Add this article to my sources and pull the quotable passages
Which sentences in this draft make a claim I have no source for?
Check every quote in this piece against its source
Are any of the links in my sources dead?
